reading.body:
Julie Fedorchak's AI record is mostly money and votes: five AI company PACs gave to her committee and she voted Yea on four AI-related bills, with no data here showing one caused the other.

The pattern is a steady flow of small contributions from the political committees of Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta, ranging from $1,000 to $5,000, alongside recorded votes on bills the data does not name by subject. The one negative entry, a $2,000 Google refund on 2025-07-31, reverses a $2,000 Google contribution from 2025-08-01, which suggests a correction rather than a new event. Two cosponsorships appear, H.R. 7968 and H.R. 633, the latter identified as the TAKE IT DOWN Act.

For AI specifically, this is the legislative and fundraising layer around the technology, not the compute layer. Nothing here concerns data centers, power contracts, or grid interconnection, so it cannot speak to whether Fedorchak has taken a position on the physical buildout that constrains AI scaling. What it does show is that AI-adjacent committees are treating her as worth funding, which is a signal of perceived relevance on tech policy.

The data does not say what any of the four voted bills would do, whether the contributions influenced any vote, or what Fedorchak has said about AI. It covers 16 dated events through 2026-08-31 and nothing else.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Julie Fedorchak: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 16 events.
